---
title: "Building models"
subtitle: "Otto & Day, chapters 2 and 3, with PracticalCAS"
engine: julia
---

Chapters 2 and 3 build the classic models from verbal descriptions: write down
what happens to individuals in one time step (or per unit time) and collect
terms. The algebra of those derivations is exactly what a CAS is for.

```{julia}
using PracticalCAS
```

## Diploid selection

With allele frequency `p`, random mating gives genotype frequencies
`p²`, `2pq`, `q²`; viability selection weights them by `WAA`, `WAa`, `Waa`.
The frequency of `A` among the survivors:

```{julia}
@syms p::(0, 1) WAA::positive WAa::positive Waa::positive
q = 1 - p
Wbar = p^2 * WAA + 2p * q * WAa + q^2 * Waa
p′ = (p^2 * WAA + p * q * WAa) / Wbar
Δp = simplify(p′ - p)
```

The change factors into `p q` times a difference of marginal fitnesses, so
`p = 0` and `p = 1` are always equilibria:

```{julia}
factor(Δp)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(Δp, p * (1 - p) * (p * (WAA - WAa) + (1 - p) * (WAa - Waa)) / Wbar)
```

With additive fitnesses `1 + s`, `1 + s/2`, `1` and weak selection, the change
per generation is approximately `s p (1 - p)/2`: the logistic equation of
continuous-time selection.

```{julia}
@syms s
Δs = subs(Δp, WAA => 1 + s, WAa => 1 + s / 2, Waa => 1)
taylor(Δs, s, 0, 1)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(taylor(Δs, s, 0, 1), s * p * (1 - p) / 2)
```

## Mutation

Alleles mutate from `A` to `a` at rate `μ` and back at rate `ν`:

```{julia}
@syms μ::(0, 1) ν::(0, 1)
mut = recurrence(p => (1 - μ) * p + ν * (1 - p))
equilibria(mut)
```

```{julia}
rsolve(mut, sym(:t; natural = true))
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(only(equilibria(mut))[p], ν / (μ + ν))
```

## Migration

An island receives a fraction `m` of migrants each generation from a mainland
where the allele frequency is `pₘ`:

```{julia}
@syms m::(0, 1) pₘ::(0, 1) t::natural p₀::(0, 1)
mig = rsolve(recurrence(p => (1 - m) * p + m * pₘ), t)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(subs(mig, t => 0), sym(:p₀; lo = 0, hi = 1))
@assert isequiv(limit(subs(mig, m => 1 // 2), t, ∞), pₘ)
```

## From discrete to continuous time

A discrete-time model with growth factor `1 + r Δt` per interval `Δt` becomes
the continuous model `dn/dt = r n` as `Δt → 0`:

```{julia}
@syms r::positive n::positive Δt::positive
limit(((1 + r * Δt) * n - n) / Δt, Δt, 0)
```

and the discrete solution `(1 + r Δt)^(t/Δt)` tends to `exp(r t)`:

```{julia}
@syms τ::positive
limit((1 + r * Δt)^(τ / Δt), Δt, 0)
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
@assert isequiv(limit(((1 + r * Δt) * n - n) / Δt, Δt, 0), r * n)
@assert isequiv(limit((1 + r * Δt)^(τ / Δt), Δt, 0), exp(r * τ))
```

## Logistic growth and its relatives

The same reasoning gives the logistic model and the discrete-time logistic,
Ricker and Beverton–Holt models; all have the equilibria `0` and `K`.

```{julia}
@syms K::positive R::positive
models = [ode(n => r * n * (1 - n / K)),
          recurrence(n => n + r * n * (1 - n / K)),
          recurrence(n => n * exp(r * (1 - n / K))),
          recurrence(n => R * n / (1 + (R - 1) * n / K))]
[sort([e[n] for e in equilibria(mod)]; by = string) for mod in models]
```

```{julia}
#| include: false
for mod in models
    @assert Set(e[n] for e in equilibria(mod)) == Set([toterm(0), K])
end
```
